learningObjective: Explain the roles of Dialect, Trait, and Interface in MLIR extensibility.

canonicalClaims.claim: Dialects are namespaces grouping Ops/Types/Attrs; Traits are compile-time metadata on Op classes for uniform static handling; Interfaces are virtual dispatch tables allowing polymorphic behavior on Ops/Types/Dialects.
conditions: Standard MLIR extensibility mechanisms as documented in LangRef.
nonImplications: Does not imply Traits can carry runtime state.
Does not imply every Op has all three artifacts.

misconceptions.claim: Traits and Interfaces are the same mechanism with different names.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Traits are static compile-time markers; Interfaces are virtual dispatch tables (runtime polymorphism).

misconceptions.claim: Dialects are exclusive: only one Dialect can exist per IRModule.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Multiple dialects coexist in one module — that is the whole point of progressive lowering.

misconceptions.claim: Cross-Dialect lowering requires manual clone-and-rewrite of every Op.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Dialect Conversion framework + patterns + interfaces replace Ops with new ones, wiring uses automatically.

misconceptions.claim: A Trait can override an Op's builder to inject runtime logic.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Traits are static; runtime behavior is handled by Interfaces or explicit Op methods.
